references.text: Both texts deal with taking a pledge from a neighbor and show respect for the poor person's dignity and need for clothing.
Deals with the prohibition against taking certain items as pledges, especially those necessary for daily living.
Part of the same legal collection concerning the fair treatment of the vulnerable in society, including widows and foreigners.
Job describes unjust pledge-taking as an evil act, highlighting the seriousness of the law in Deuteronomy.
Proverbs warns against putting up security for another, related to the theme of loans and pledges.
Ezekiel describes the righteous person as one who returns the pledge, in line with the spirit of this law.
Ezekiel mentions unjust pledge-taking as a sin, showing the importance of this law.
Amos condemns those who take clothing as a pledge, thereby violating the spirit of the law on fair pledge-taking.
